description: Fetch details for a batch of specified accessible cloud agents by bcIds. Users and service accounts can fetch their own runs. Team admins can additionally fetch teammates' runs only when enabled in team MCP settings. When matching agents are found, writes basic run info to index.json under a unique /tmp/cursor/cloud-agent-transcripts/<datetime-id>/ run directory, and can optionally write per-agent diff-metadata.json, setup-logs.txt, start-logs.txt, environment-info.json, events.json, and transcript.json files. Set includeEvents to include each run's dashboard events. First-class Task results include cloudAgentBcId, which can be passed to another batch-fetch-details call. Returns the run directory and written paths; transcripts can be very large, so read them via subagents, never directly.

bcIds.description: Agent ids to fetch as a batch (max 50). Each id is access-checked and constrained to this run's environment (or, when this run has no saved environment, to agents on the same repository).

includeDiffMetadata.description: Also write each agent's PR link/status and change counts to diff-metadata.json. Defaults to false.

includeSetupLogs.description: Also write each agent's pod setup and image-build logs to setup-logs.txt. Defaults to false.

includeStartLogs.description: Also write each agent's start-command stdout/stderr/exit lines to start-logs.txt (filtered from the same Redis setup stream as includeSetupLogs; includes system starts like exec-daemon interleaved with the user start script). Defaults to false.

includeEnvironment.description: Also write each agent's environment identity/config and egress policy to environment-info.json. Defaults to false.

includeEvents.description: Also write each agent's dashboard events to events.json. Defaults to false.

includeTranscripts.description: Also write each requested agent's full conversation to <bcId>/transcript.json. First-class Task tool results include cloudAgentBcId, which can be passed to a subsequent batch-fetch-details call. Defaults to false.

description: Fetch the install/setup logs for one environment build by buildId (bld-<YYYYMMDD>-<uuid>, as surfaced by environment-info's build block). Returns the log text inline (large outputs are spilled to a file automatically by the MCP framework). Logs cover the build's Docker image build plus clone/install/setup output and are retained for ~10 days after the build; older builds (or builds from before build-log capture shipped) return a retention note with no log body. Only builds of this run's own environment are accessible.

buildId.description: The environment build id to fetch install/setup logs for (e.g. bld-20260709-<uuid>).

description: Return the current cloud-agent run's environment (name, environment & version public ids, source, how/when it was recorded, repos, the full environment.json, a link to the environment in the cursor.com dashboard, and environmentDeleted when the linked environment is soft-deleted), a top-level `repos` array of canonical repository URLs (the same strings as `environment.repos` and the values `trigger-environment-build` `refs[].repoUrl` must match; still set when `environment` is null, from composer.repoUrl), the effective egress policy (allow-all, the complete merged allowed-domain list, or unresolved with a reason), the environment build the pod booted from (build id, snapshot id, git-setup mode, warm-fork mode) or null when the run started just-in-time rather than from a build, and (for internal runs) the initiating Cursor client build info (version + commit SHA, same as Help → About). Use top-level `repos` when choosing `refs[].repoUrl`. Use `environmentJsonPath` to tell repo-file managed environments from db-backed ones: a present path (defaulting to `.cursor/environment.json`) means the config is read from that repository environment.json (repo-file managed), while a null/absent path means a db-backed snapshot config (db-managed). When environmentDeleted is true, treat the environment as historical only — do not trigger new builds or treat the environment id as live.

Look up one Cursor automation by its id (UUID). Calls the AutomationsService GetAutomation API as the current run's principal and returns AutomationInfo metadata, enforcing the same read-access rules as the automations dashboard: automation id, name, enabled state, display owner/creator, owner email, and URL when readable; the same metadata fields for a teammate's private automation when only a restricted summary is visible; a not-found error otherwise (including when the automation exists but is not accessible).

id.description: The automation's id, a UUID (e.g. 6e0d261c-86a2-4383-89f0-9162c1c10662). Find it in the automation's dashboard URL or in AutomationsService responses.

description: Return the list of events recorded for the current cloud-agent run — the same events shown on the run's cursor.com dashboard page — ordered oldest first. Events cover run lifecycle and setup outcomes (e.g. setup warnings, follow-up limits) and soft failures such as MCP authentication errors (kind `mcp_auth_error`: an MCP server rejected this run's credentials, so its tool calls failed while the run continued). Each event has publicId, createdAtMs, category (build | agent_setup | agent_run), logLevel (info | warn | error), a stable machine-readable kind, a user-facing title, and optional detail and linkUrl.

Return a point-in-time snapshot of THIS run's user-visible pending follow-up message queue — the same queue shown on the dashboard. No arguments; always scoped to this run. The currently executing message is no longer queued. Defer slow testing and verification while queued messages remain, then verify the cumulative result when the queue is empty. Returns hasQueuedMessages, queuedMessageCount, and queued message metadata (followupId, createdAtMs, source, text). Does not include attachments or internal queue entries.

List cloud agents accessible to the current run's principal in this run's environment (or, for a run without a saved environment, agents on the same repository), ordered by creation time (newest first). Users and service accounts see their own runs. Team admins can additionally browse teammates' runs only when enabled in team MCP settings. Returns basic run metadata plus URLs. Filters: source, lifecycle status, setup status, recency/creation windows, archived, self-hosted, code changes, and pull-request creation. Paging: limit (default 50, max 200) + offset; the response includes returned, offset, limit, hasMore, nextOffset when more accessible agents were found, and totalMatched only when the accessible scan is complete. With many cloud agents, narrow with filters before paging through everything.

sources.description: Filter by agent source category, matching the source field returned in results. One or more of: desktop, web, mobile, slack, linear, scm, cli, sand, setup, sdk, automations, api, bugbot_autofix, qabot_frontend, local, internal.

statuses.description: Filter by lifecycle status(es), matching the status field returned in results.

setupStatus.description: Filter by user install setup status. INSTALL_FAILED indicates a confirmed failure, INSTALL_SUCCEEDED indicates a confirmed success, and INSTALL_STARTED indicates that setup started without a recorded outcome. null means no status was recorded and does not establish success or failure. Omit this field to apply no setup-status filter.

includeArchived.description: Include archived/killed agents. Defaults to false.

activeSince.description: Only include agents with activity at or after this ISO-8601 UTC instant. Omitted by default.

createdAfter.description: Only include agents created at or after this ISO-8601 UTC instant.

createdBefore.description: Only include agents created at or before this ISO-8601 UTC instant.

isSelfHostedWorker.description: Filter by where the agent runs: true for self-hosted private-worker agents, false for managed public-cloud agents, omit for both.

didMakeCodeChanges.description: Filter by whether the agent made code changes (committed or not): true for agents with a recorded non-zero diff (files/lines changed), false for agents with no recorded changes, omit for both.

didCreatePullRequest.description: Filter by whether the agent created a pull request: true for agents with a PR, false for agents without one, omit for both.

limit.description: Max number of agents to return (default 50, max 200).

offset.description: Number of matched accessible agents to skip before this page. Use the nextOffset from a previous response to page. Note: not a stable cursor — results are re-fetched and re-sorted each call, so offsets can shift if agents change between calls.

description: List this run's environment builds — the prebuilt environment snapshots a cloud agent can boot from instead of running install from scratch — newest first, so build ids can be found for environment-build-logs. Each entry carries buildId, status (IN_PROGRESS, SUCCEEDED, FAILED), failureType, source, triggerType, environmentVersionId, userFacingSnapshotId, createdAtMs, and completedAtMs. Filters: statuses, createdAfter, createdBefore. Paging: limit (default 25, max 100); when hasMore is true, pass the response's opaque nextCursor back as cursor to fetch the next (older) page. Builds exist only for environments that have environment builds enabled; a run with no linked environment returns an empty list.

statuses.description: Filter by build outcome. One or more of: IN_PROGRESS, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELLED, SKIPPED.

createdAfter.description: Only include builds created at or after this ISO-8601 UTC instant.

createdBefore.description: Only include builds created strictly before this ISO-8601 UTC instant.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor: pass the previous response's nextCursor to fetch the next (older) page.

description: List the self-hosted workers (`cursor worker start` machines) currently connected and accessible to this run's principal, so a cloud agent can pick one to target. A worker only appears while its worker process is running and registered. Access matches the dashboard: personal workers are visible to their owner, and team-pool workers to team admins or to a caller already using them. Each row carries workerId, displayName, machineDisplayName, machineId, repos, labels, isInUse, activeBcId, teamId, and connectedAtMs, plus two derived fields: sharedAssignmentAllowed (the worker multiplexes several agents at once, so targeting it runs concurrently rather than queueing) and eligibleForSubagent (a subagent could be placed on it right now without waiting for a claim — true for shared workers even while busy, false for an in-use exclusive pool worker). Filters: status (all, idle, in_use) and scope (all, team_pool, personal). Paging: limit (default 50, max 100) + offset; the response includes returned, offset, limit, totalCount, hasMore, and nextOffset. There is no OS, arch, CPU, or memory information — a worker's capabilities are expressed only through its labels.

status.description: Filter by whether a worker is currently running a cloud agent. Defaults to all.

scope.description: Which workers to return: personal self-hosted machines, the team's Self-Hosted Pool, or both. Defaults to all.

offset.description: Number of workers to skip before returning results. Use with limit to page.

description: Return the current cloud-agent run identity, basic run metadata (including lifecycle and setup status), and the URL where the run is available (https://cursor.com/agents/<bcId>).

Start one DRAFT environment build of this run's own environment (fresh git checkout + install script, snapshotted at the end). OK to call during environment setup to validate the config before proposing, or when the user asks to trigger a build. Each build boots a pod and runs the full install for up to a few hours, so do not trigger casually outside setup. By default every repo in the environment builds at its default branch; pass `refs` (per repoUrl) to build specific branches/tags/SHAs — every repoUrl must belong to this run's environment. Note: for db-managed environments, a build created from a non-default ref can be tested but cannot be promoted to active later — only builds from every repo's default branch are promotable, so omit `refs` if you want a promotable build. Pass `environmentJson` to build with a custom config instead of the environment's saved db-backed config. For a greenfield run with no linked environment, `environmentJson` is required and creates a personal transitional draft automatically. The config is recorded durably on the build and never changes active environment settings. `environmentJson` is not supported for repo-file managed environments (those whose config is read from a repository environment.json — see `environmentJsonPath` in environment-info) and is rejected for them; test repo-file environments by building off a branch instead — create a branch, edit its environment.json, and build that branch via `refs`. Draft builds never become the build new agents boot from and skip warm-pool seeding, so they are safe for experiments; they appear in list-environment-builds (source AGENT, trigger MANUAL) and their logs are fetchable with environment-build-logs. Returns the new buildId immediately; the build runs in the background. Limited to a few in-flight builds per environment.

repoUrl.description: Repository URL matching one of environment-info's top-level `repos` (same strings as environment.repos).

ref.description: Branch, tag, or commit SHA to build this repo at.

refs.description: Per-repository ref overrides. Every repoUrl must belong to this run's environment; repos left out build at their default branch.

install.description: Idempotent repository bootstrap command run from /workspace after checkout (and when refreshing dependencies). Must terminate; use for dependency install and source-derived generation, not long-running servers, migrations, or tests. Prefer one command per line rather than chaining with &&.

start.description: Command run on each container start after install. Use for per-boot service startup with a non-daemonizing process (for example a dev server that stays attached). Do not use for dependency install or one-time setup.

snapshot.description: Saved base-environment snapshot ID. One of build, image, or snapshot typically defines the environment base.

environmentJson.description: environment.json object used instead of the environment's saved db-backed config for this draft build. Property schema is authoritative (install, start, and optional snapshot). The override replaces saved config wholesale for the build, so include snapshot when the build should start from a READY take-environment-snapshot base. Required when this run has no linked environment (creates a personal transitional draft). Recorded on the build only; does not change active environment settings. Not supported for repo-file managed environments (see environmentJsonPath in environment-info)—test those via branch refs instead.

inputSchema.description: Trigger a draft build for this run's environment. If the current run has no environment returned from environment-info, environmentJson is required.
